projects.title: Autonomous Drone Swarm Perception & Obstacle Avoidance
projects.shortDescription: Decentralized multi-UAV path planning and real-time obstacle avoidance utilizing ROS 2, LiDAR-inertial odometry, and edge neural networks.
projects.fullDescription:
This project introduces a robust, fault-tolerant decentralized perception and collision avoidance architecture designed for quadcopter swarms operating in GPS-denied cluttered environments. Using lightweight 3D LiDAR point cloud processing and onboard stereoscopic depth cameras, each drone generates real-time OctoMap voxel representations and communicates state vectors via peer-to-peer Wi-Fi mesh protocols.

The trajectory optimization module integrates minimum-snap polynomials with distributed model predictive control (DMPC), guaranteeing safe clearances even in dense foliage and urban canyons. Benchmarked across both Gazebo PX4 SITL simulations and custom carbon-fiber quadrotors equipped with Jetson Orin Nano companion computers.
features: Real-time 3D LiDAR FAST-LIO2 point cloud slam with sub-5cm positional drift
Decentralized DMPC trajectory coordination preventing swarm inter-collision
Onboard edge inference running YOLOv8-tiny on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano at 45 FPS
Dynamic mesh networking maintaining heartbeat over IEEE 802.11s mesh routers
Fail-safe autonomous return-to-home (RTH) upon radio link loss or low battery
requirements: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano / Xavier or x86 companion computer with Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
ROS 2 Humble Hawksbill installation with FastDDS middleware
Mid-360 Livox LiDAR or Intel RealSense D435i depth sensor
PX4 Autopilot Firmware v1.14 or later on Pixhawk 6C / Holybro flight controller
projects.installation:
### 1. Clone the Repository
git clone https://github.com/limo-hub/autonomous-drone-swarm.git
cd autonomous-drone-swarm

### 2. Install ROS 2 Dependencies
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
rosdep update
rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src -r -y

### 3. Build Swarm Workspace with Colcon
colcon build --symlink-install --cmake-args -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
source install/setup.bash
projects.usage:
### Launch Simulation in Gazebo
ros2 launch swarm_bringup multi_uav_gazebo.launch.py num_drones:=4

### Run Decentralized Swarm Controller
ros2 launch swarm_control dmpc_coordinator.launch.py
projects.documentation:
# Architecture & Data Flow

The system employs a layered decoupled architecture:
1. **Sensory Abstraction Layer**: Interfaces with hardware drivers via micro-ROS.
2. **State Estimation**: Fuses IMU measurements with Livox Mid-360 point clouds using an iterated Kalman filter.
3. **Spatial Representation**: Feeds point clouds into a dynamic spatial Octree with decay counters to prune transient obstacles.
4. **Trajectory Generator**: Solves convex optimization problems iteratively every 50ms to yield dynamically feasible polynomial trajectories.

## Communication Matrix
| Stream | Frequency | Transport | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drone State | 20 Hz | UDP Broadcast | Pose, Velocity, Bounds |
| Collision Buffer | 10 Hz | FastDDS | Spatial bounding spheres |
| Video Stream | 30 Hz | RTSP | H.264 Compressed Feed |

projects.title: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) & BB84 Simulator
projects.shortDescription: High-fidelity quantum optical cryptography simulator implementing the BB84 protocol, decoy-state analysis, and Eve intercept-resend noise modeling.
projects.fullDescription:
As quantum computers advance toward Shor algorithm cryptanalysis, post-quantum key exchange mechanisms are paramount. This engineering project simulates end-to-end Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) via the BB84 polarization protocol and continuous-variable quantum channels.

Built in Python and Rust using Qiskit and NumPy, the suite models single-photon sources, fiber birefringence, detector dark counts, and beam splitters. It provides comprehensive decoy-state mathematical bounds to thwart photon-number-splitting (PNS) attacks by potential eavesdroppers ("Eve"), enabling engineering students to compute Quantum Bit Error Rates (QBER) and secret key extraction rates interactively.
features: Exact polarization state preparation using computational (|0>, |1>) and Hadamard (|+>, |->) bases
Statistical modeling of fiber attenuation at 1550nm telecom wavelength
Simulation of active eavesdropping (Intercept-Resend and Photon-Number Splitting)
Cascade error correction algorithm implementation with privacy amplification hashing
WebAssembly interactive graphical UI for real-time photon exchange inspection
requirements: Python 3.10+ or Rust toolchain 1.75+
Qiskit v1.0.0+ with Aer simulator provider
NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib for mathematical modeling
projects.installation:
### Python Virtual Environment Setup
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # Or on Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

### Rust Engine Compilation
cd rust_core
cargo build --release --lib
projects.usage:
### Run Monte Carlo QKD Simulation
python -m qkd_core.cli --pulses 100000 --channel-length-km 50 --dark-count-rate 1e-6 --eve-ratio 0.15
projects.documentation:
# BB84 Protocol Flow
1. **Alice prepares random photon states**: Chooses random bits (0, 1) and random bases (Rectilinear +, Diagonal x).
2. **Quantum Channel Transmission**: Photons propagate through fiber optic channel with exponential loss: T = 10^(-alpha * L / 10).
3. **Bob measures states**: Randomly selects measurement basis (+, x).
4. **Sifting Stage**: Alice and Bob communicate their bases over public classical channel and discard mismatched trials.
5. **Error Estimation**: Subsample revealed to calculate QBER:
   - If QBER < 11%, privacy amplification yields unconditional secrecy.
   - If QBER >= 11%, channel is aborted due to suspected eavesdropping.

projects.title: Bionic Myoelectric 6-DOF Prosthetic Hand with Sensory Feedback
projects.shortDescription: 3D printed multi-articulated prosthetic limb actuated by miniature linear servos and governed by multi-channel surface EMG pattern recognition.
projects.fullDescription:
Modern bionic prosthetics remain prohibitively expensive for most amputees. This engineering project presents an open-architecture, low-cost 6-Degree-of-Freedom (6-DOF) bionic hand featuring proportional grip force control, haptic sensory vibration feedback, and real-time EMG gesture recognition.

The mechanical chassis is optimized for lightweight FDM carbon-fiber composite printing with compliant flexure finger joints. Four dry-contact Ag/AgCl skin electrodes capture differential forearm muscle potentials, amplified via instrumental amplifiers and processed on an ESP32-S3 microcontroller using TinyML convolutional neural nets running directly on the edge.
features: 6 individually actuated finger servos providing cylindrical, pinch, tripod, and point grips
TinyML edge gesture classifier recognizing 8 distinct hand postures at 96.4% accuracy
Sub-120ms actuation latency from muscle contraction trigger to physical grasp
FSR tip pressure sensors mapped to ERM vibrotactile feedback motors on upper arm
USB-C programmable with Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) smartphone configuration app
requirements: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 DevKit or custom PCB
6x micro linear coreless servos (6V operating voltage)
MyoWare 2.0 or AD8232 custom analog EMG conditioning front-end
3D printer with minimum 200x200x200mm build volume using PETG or PLA-CF
projects.installation:
### 1. 3D Print Components
Export STL files from /cad directory and slice at 0.16mm layer height with 40% gyroid infill.

### 2. Flash ESP32 Firmware
Use PlatformIO in VS Code:
pio run --target upload
projects.usage:
### Calibration Mode
Hold button S1 for 3 seconds to initiate 5-step muscle calibration:
Relaxed -> Fist -> Spread -> Pinch -> Point.
projects.documentation:
# Electrical Wiring & Pinout
- GPIO 14: EMG Channel 1 (Flexor carpi radialis)
- GPIO 15: EMG Channel 2 (Extensor digitorum)
- GPIO 18-23: PWM servo output signals (50 Hz pulse trains)
- GPIO 4: I2C SDA for fingertip tactile bus

projects.title: Decentralized Smart Grid Microgrid & EV Dynamic Charging Optimizer
projects.shortDescription: Industrial IoT smart grid telemetry simulator forecasting renewable energy peaks and orchestrating bidirectional V2G (Vehicle-to-Grid) load balancing.
projects.fullDescription:
High penetration of intermittent photovoltaics and electric vehicle charging presents severe stability challenges to municipal electrical distribution networks. This project delivers an automated demand-response and microgrid orchestration system using Transformer-based temporal forecasting and reinforcement learning.

The system gathers high-frequency voltage, frequency, and phase phasor measurement unit (PMU) data across IEEE 33-bus distribution networks, simulating dynamic price incentives and balancing stationary lithium-ion BESS (Battery Energy Storage Systems) against thousands of parked EV charging sessions.
features: IEEE 33-bus power flow simulation executing Newton-Raphson iterations under 10ms
Bidirectional V2G charging schedule minimizing substation transformer thermal stress
Reinforcement learning PPO agent dispatching local battery reserves during price spikes
OpenTelemetry and Apache Kafka ingesting 50,000 telemetry points per second
Interactive real-time SVG grid topology visualization with heatmaps
requirements: Docker & Docker Compose
Python 3.11 with PyTorch & Pandapower library
Kafka cluster or Redpanda instance
projects.installation:
### Quickstart with Docker Compose
docker-compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d
python scripts/seed_grid_topology.py
projects.usage:
### Run Microgrid Balancing Simulation
python -m grid_optimizer.simulate --scenario extreme_solar_duck_curve --hours 48
projects.documentation:
# Power Flow Formulation
The bus admittance matrix Y_bus is solved iteratively to ensure voltage magnitudes remain within 0.95 to 1.05 p.u. per ANSI C84.1 standards.

projects.title: eBPF-Powered Real-Time Linux Threat Detection & Zero-Trust Agent
projects.shortDescription: Kernel-level telemetry collector leveraging Extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) to detect rootkits, privilege escalations, and unauthorized container escapes.
projects.fullDescription:
Traditional user-space endpoint detection agents suffer from high CPU overhead and vulnerability to sophisticated kernel rootkits. This project implements a zero-overhead, non-invasive threat surveillance system operating inside the Linux kernel via eBPF kprobes, tracepoints, and LSM (Linux Security Modules) hooks.

Events such as unexpected `execve`, raw socket creation, ptrace process injection, and container namespace jumping are intercepted in kernel space and streamed via ring buffers to a Rust user-space daemon for behavioral anomaly scoring against the MITRE ATT&CK matrix.
features: Kernel-level hook verification preventing malicious syscall tampering without rebooting
High-performance BPF ring buffers minimizing packet drop at 100k events/sec
Automated process tree lineage reconstruction to track parent-child process ancestry
Pre-compiled CO-RE (Compile Once – Run Everywhere) binaries across Linux kernels 5.8 to 6.8
Exportable Prometheus metrics and structured JSON audit logs for SIEM integration
requirements: Linux kernel 5.8 or newer with BTF (BPF Type Format) enabled
Root or CAP_BPF / CAP_PERFMON privileges to load BPF programs
Rust 1.77+ with bpf-linker
projects.installation:
### Build with Cargo Aya
cargo install bpf-linker
cargo xtask build-ebpf --release
cargo build --release
projects.usage:
### Run Threat Hunter Daemon
sudo ./target/release/limo-threat-hunter --filter-namespaces --alert-level high
projects.documentation:
# Architecture of the Kernel Monitor
eBPF programs run in a sandboxed virtual machine within the Linux kernel verified for memory safety before execution.

projects.title: Decentralized Cold-Chain Supply Chain Provenance with Zero-Knowledge Proofs
projects.shortDescription: Verifiable pharmaceutical cold-chain provenance tracker integrating IoT temperature sensors, Ethereum Layer-2 rollups, and zk-SNARKs for trade secret preservation.
projects.fullDescription:
Pharmaceutical supply chains require unbroken temperature tracking without exposing sensitive supplier pricing, volume, or route telemetry. This project implements a hybrid architecture combining cryptographic zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs with Circom) and IoT temperature data loggers.

Shipment carriers submit cryptographic commitments that temperature remained within the critical 2°C to 8°C corridor throughout transit without revealing precise GPS coordinates or intermediate stops, guaranteeing compliance before smart contracts automatically release escrow payments.
features: Circom 2.1 zk-SNARK circuits generating groth16 proofs under 1.2 seconds in browser
Smart contracts deployed on Arbitrum Sepolia Layer-2 for sub-cent transaction costs
Tamper-evident cryptographic state hashes signed by hardware security modules (HSM)
Automated automated escrow settlement upon verifiable proof validation
Decentralized IPFS metadata storage for compliance inspection certificates
requirements: Node.js 18+ and Rust toolchain
Circom compiler v2.1.6 and snarkjs
Hardhat or Foundry for Solidity smart contract compilation
projects.installation:
### 1. Compile zk Circuits
cd circuits
circom temperature_proof.circom --r1cs --wasm --sym
snarkjs groth16 setup temperature_proof.r1cs pot14_final.ptau circuit_0000.zkey

### 2. Compile Smart Contracts
cd ../contracts
npx hardhat compile
projects.usage:
### Run Integration Tests
npx hardhat test
projects.documentation:
# Cryptographic Circuit Constraints
The circuit verifies that for an array of N temperature points T[i], each value satisfies MinThreshold <= T[i] <= MaxThreshold without publishing the array T.

projects.title: Quantum Annealing Traffic Flow Optimization for Megacities
projects.shortDescription: QUBO (Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) formulation solving real-time urban traffic congestion using D-Wave quantum annealer APIs.
projects.fullDescription: Traffic congestion in global metropolitan areas incurs billions in lost productivity and fuel consumption. This project translates dynamic multi-agent vehicular routing into Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) graphs solvable on D-Wave Advantage quantum annealers and hybrid quantum-classical solvers.
features: QUBO conversion of 10,000 intersecting road graph nodes into binary spin matrices
Benchmarked against Dijkstra and A* algorithms demonstrating 38% reduction in bottleneck formation
Continuous hybrid classical-quantum cloud orchestration
requirements: Python 3.10+
dwave-ocean-sdk
networkx
projects.documentation:
# Mathematical QUBO Mapping
Minimizes the overlap function of pairwise routes weighted by road capacity and travel duration.

comments.content: Incredible work on the FAST-LIO2 integration! I tested this with our university Pixhawk 6C setup and the point cloud synchronization is remarkably smooth. Have you benchmarked latency with more than 8 drones?
Thanks Elena! Yes, with up to 12 drones in Gazebo, the mesh communications bandwidth stays under 1.8 Mbps per node. We plan to release the 12-UAV benchmark dataset in the next minor version.
The 3D print tolerances for the flexure joints are spot on. Highly recommended for any student robotics lab looking to get started with EMG prosthetics!
